cells.remarks: —undated The record, in characters of about the 7-8th century A. D., contains two parts. The epigraph was erected by Srīpāla, grandson of Dharana-gāmuṇḍa, and disciple of Prabhā[chandra?] of Paralūra-gaṇa. It further records a grant of wet land to the west of Karmmagere (?), for the benefit of the Jinālaya, by Dōṇa-gāmuṇḍa and others with the permission of Mādhavatti when Sindarasa was governing Gangi-Pāṇḍivura. Now preserved in the Kannada Research Institute at Dharwar.

cells.location: SAUNDATTI, PARASGAD TALUK, BELGAUM DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: On a slab set up in the Basti-guḍi
cells.dynasty: Krishṇa II · Kṛishṇa II
cells.language: Sanskrit and Kannada
cells.remarks: The inscription in Sanskrit and Kannada language is dated in Śaka 797, Manmatha, but is engraved in characters of about the 11th or 12th century A. D. The Śaka and the cyclic year correspond to A. D. 875-76. It records a grant of eighteen nivartanas of land by Mahāsāmanta Prithvirāma, the son Mērada, to a Jinēndra-bhavana got built by himself. The donee is stated to be the disciple of Indrakīrtisvāmin who in turn was the disciple of Guṇakīrti-munīśvara. The latter again was the disciple of Muḷḷabhaṭṭa of Mailāpatīrtha and Kārēyagaṇa. Lines 1 to 4 record a later grant, made by Kanna, of six nivartanas of land in the sīvaṭa Mulgunda in Sugandhavartti-12. Lines 18-19 state that the grant made by Prithvīrāma was renewed by Kārttavirya and (his wife) Bhāgalāmbikā on the occasion of a solar eclipse. The donors of all the grants are of the Raṭṭa family, Mērada being the first member. Text1

cells.remarks: The record is dated Śaka 902, Vikrama, Paushya, śu. 10, Thursday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṅkrānti. The Saṅkrānti occurred on Thursday, December 23, A. D. 980. The tithi was, however, śu. 14 on that day and not śu. 10 as stated in the record. The inscription registers the grant of 150 mattars of land by the Raṭṭa chief Śāntivarmarasa to the Jaina monastery (basadi) caused to be constructed by him at Sugandhavarti (i. e., modern Saundatti). The genealogy of this chief is given. The gift was entrusted to Bāhubali-bhaṭṭāraka. It also records another gift of 150 mattars of land by the chief’s mother Nijiyabbarasi to the same monastery. The record is published in JBBRAS. Vol. X, p. 204. 1. Continuation is worn out.

The record gives a genealogical account of the Chālukya dynasty in the beginning commencing from Raṇarāga, son of Jayasiṁha I, and ending with Vasudhaikamalla Ayyaṇadēva. It registers a gift of 60 mattars of land, three gardens, one oil-mill and three shops, by Mahāsāmanta Dēvaṇarasa described as the brother of the king, to god Nagarēśvara. Moraḍiya Chāmuṇḍayya, the Sēnabōva, wrote the record. It mentions Chandraśēkharāchārya of the Nagarēśvara temple and also certain other individuals.

cells.remarks: This badly damaged record is dated Śaka 991, Kīlaka, Amāvāsyā, Sunday, Dakshiṇāyana [saṁkrānti]. This date is irregular. The cyclic year corresponding to the given Śaka year was Saumya and not Kilaka. The intended date seems to be A. D. 1069, June 21 when the tithi was amāvāsyā and the week-day was Sunday. The Saṁkrānti, however, occurred three days later. The inscription records the gift of certain money incomes made by Mādhavayya Nāyaka with the permission of the king for the benefit of the temple of Nakharēśvara at Rūvige when Pāyyarasa was governing Tardavāḍi division. The inscription also refers to another gift of oil made by the Fifty Telliga tenants for a lamp in the temple of Kēdārēśvara of the place (i. e., Rūvige) in the year Śaka 967, Pārtthiva, Pushya śu. 5, Sunday Uttarāyaṇa-Saṁkrānti. This date corresponds to A. D. 1045, December 15, Sunday, f. d. t.·64. There was no Saṁkrānti on this date. It appears that this gift was revived as in the case of No. 45 below.

cells.dynasty: Bhuvanaikamalla (Sōmēśvara II) · Sōmēśvara II
cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: This record is dated Śaka 994, Paushya, śu. 11, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṁkrānti corresponding regularly to A. D. 1072, December 24. The inscription records the revival of the endowment of the village Guḍigēre, formerly made by Kumkumamahādēvi, the younger sister of the Chālukya king Vijayāditya, to Ānesejjeya-basadi which was caused to be constructed by her a Puligere. The gift is stated to have been made by queen Kamchalamahādēvi who was governing from the headquarters at Muḷugunda and others in the presence of the king, with the consent of Bhāskara-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya on the occasion of his victorious return from the northern expedition. It is also stated that Mahāpradhāna Daṇḍanāyaka Rudrabhaṭṭōpādhyāya was administering Guḍigēre and Daṇḍanāyaka Īśvarabhaṭṭa was in charge of all the departments. The donee was Nandi-paṇḍitadēva.

cells.dynasty: Bhuvanaikamalla (Sōmēśvara II) · Sōmēśvara II
cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: The record is dated Śaka 998, Rākshasa, Pushya, Amāvāsya, Sunday, Hasta nakshatra, Uttarāyaṇa-saṃkrānti. The details of this date are irregular. The Śaka year 998 corresponded to the Cyclic year Anala when the said saṃkrānti occurred on Saturday, the tithi being ba. 11 of the month Pushya and the nakshatra Viśākhā. In the cyclic year Rākshasa the saṃkrānti occurred on Friday the tithi being śu. 15 and the nakshatra Punarvasu. The intended date might be 1076 A.D., December 24, Saturday. The inscription registers the gift of the village Puḷḷavaḷa situated to the south of the river Varadā in Bāsavura-140, a sub-division of Banavāsi-12,000, to God Svayambhū Sōmēśvara of Kalkēre, for worship and offerings to the deity and for feeding the ascetics, etc., by Bhuvanaikamalla-Vira-Noḷamba who was governing Noḷambavāḍi, Pānumgaḷḷu-nāḍu and Banavāsidēśa. The gift was made, in conjunction with his wife Māḷaladēvi, at the request of Perggaḍe Divākara and was entrusted to Dēvasinga Jīya. The king was at that time camping at Baṅkāpura. The record contains an eulogy of the donor and his wife.

The tithi, however, was śu. 2 and not śu. 7. The inscription records gifts of land for the benefit of the temple of Chaṇḍēśvara at Kumbiṭṭage, by Mahāsāmanta Siṁgarasa of Siyaḷāra family and Udāyādityarasa. It also records gifts of land, garden and oil to the same temple and also to the temple of Vināyaka and Ādityadēva by Kētaladēvi, queen of Tribhuvanamalladēva. The latter is said to have been ruling from his camping place at Poṇuguppe.

D. 1077 July 5. There is a second date in the record the details of which are Śaka 1000, Kālayukta, Madhumāsa (Chaitra) Amāvāsya, Sunday. This corresponds to A. D. 1078, April 14. Saturday, on which day the tithi ended at 90. This inscription records the death of Śrīnandi-Paṇḍitadēva of Sūrastra-gaṇa by the rite of Sallēkhanā observed for one month at Anesejjeya-basadi at Purikaranagara. It also records the death on the second date of Bhāskaranandi-Paṇḍita who is said to have been the elder brother of the former.

cells.remarks: The record is dated the cyclic year Durmati, Pushya, ba. Bhrigu-shashṭhi, Uttarāyaṇa-Saṃkrānti corresponding to A.D. 1081, December 24. The inscription, which is incomplete, registers a grant made by Dōṇa, the younger brother of Mahāsāmantādhipati Eremayya who was administering the Purigere-300, for the Jaina cult in Purikara. The gift was entrusted to Narēndrasēna (II), of the Sēna-gaṇa in the Mūla-saṅgha, the disciple of Nayasēna Sūri who in his turn was the disciple of Narēndrasēna (I). It is stated that at the time of the record the king's younger brother Yuvarāja Jayasiṃha (III) was governing the two Six-Hundreds (viz. Beḷvola-300 and Purigere-300), Baṇavāsi-12,000, Saṇtalige-1000 and Kandūr-1,000. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XVI, pp. 58 ff.

cells.dynasty: Tribhuvanamalla (Vikramāditya VI) · Vikramāditya VI

cells.remarks: The record is dated Vira-Vikrama, i.e., Chālukya-Vikrama year 21, Dhātu, Pushya ba. 13, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. The details given are irregular. The tithi corresponds to January 14, Wednesday, A.D. 1097. But in the next year, i.e. A.D. 1098, the tithi corresponds to January 3, when the weekday was Sunday. In neither case did the said Saṁkrānti occur. The latter date, viz., A.D. 1098, January 3 might be the intended date. The inscription records a gift, by the king, of land in Kāreyabāgu village to the temple of Jinēndra built by Kālasēna of the Raṭṭa family. It further records another gift of land by the Raṭṭa chief Sēna II to the same temple. It also refers to a gift of land made by the Raṭṭa chief Kannakaira II to his guru Kanakaprabhasiddhāntadēva. Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kārtavīrya is mentioned as the feudatory of the king. Published in JBBRAS, Vol. X, pp. 195-98.

cells.remarks: This record is dated Chālukya-Vikrama year 34, Virōdhin, Mārggaśira, Puṇṇame, Monday, lunar eclipse, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti. The details are irregular. The saṁkrānti occurred on Saturday, December 25, A. D. 1109, when the tithi was Puṣhya, śu. 2. The eclipse occurred on November 9, Tuesday when the tithi was Kārttika puṇṇame. The intended date might be A. D. 1109, November 8, Monday, f.d.t., 53. The inscription records a remission of taxes on the land (aruvaṇa) of the temple of Svayambhudēva at Khēḍa in the One Thousand division, by Lakshmīdhara-Bhaṭṭōpādhyāya, who was the preceptor of Yuvarāja Mallikārjunadēva, the eldest son of the king, who was then governing over the Tarddavāḍi1000 division. It further registers gifts of money income, taxes, etc., to the same temple by Mahāpradhāna, Permāḍiyarasa, Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Gōvaṇarasa of the Śilāra family whose genealogy also is given and by the Five Hundred Svāmis of Ayyāvoḷe and the Eight nāḍus.

In the cyclic year Subhakṛit which, however, corresponds to Śaka 1044, no solar eclipse occurred whereas in the previous year Plava, a solar eclipse occurred in the month of Phālguṇa when the weekday was Friday. The intended date may be, therefore, A.D. 1122, March 10, Friday. The inscription which falls in the reign-period of Vikramāditya VI, registers a gift of land, garden and money to god Mūlasthāna of the agrahāra Kisuvare by several individuals whose names are specified. In the beginning it seems to refer to [Jaya]kēśidēva of the Kadamba family who, it is known, was a feudatory of Vikramāditya VI.

The inscription states that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Gōvaṇadēvarasa attacked the sarvanamasya-agrahāra Cheṭṭurage, while administering the country in conjunction with twelve nāyakas from his capital at Kannavaḷḷi; killed the dāyādas there and established his uninterrupted rule. It records a gift of income from taxes due to his family, i.e. Seḷara-kula, from that village to the mahājanas of that place.
Gōvaṇadēvarasa is mentioned as the servant of Jagadēkamalla.

cells.remarks: This damaged record is dated in the regnal year of the king which is lost. The extant details of the date are Puṣya, Amāvāsyā, Monday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkrānti, solar eclipse. During the reign of this king, the eclipse occurred on the said tithi, in A. D. 1144, December 22, which might be the probable date of this record. The weekday was, however, Tuesday. The inscription contains a second date, the only available details of which are Āṣāḍha, Amāvāsyā. The inscription seems to record a gift of land, house-sites, and shop to god Gavaṛēśvaradēva of the agrahāra of Savasi (also referred to as Tapasi-grāma) by the Four-Hundred Mahājanas who are praised in the beginning. It also records a gift of income from certain taxes by the Five-Hundred Svāmis of Ayyāvoḷe and the One Thousand Tambuligas to the same deity, made over to Īśānaśakti-paṇḍita, an ācārya of the Kāḷāmukha sect. The record which contains an eulogy of these svāmis seems to register another gift on the second date. But the details are all lost.

The inscription contains a second date, the only available details of which are Āṣāḍha, Amāvāsyā.
The inscription seems to record a gift of land, house-sites, and shop to god Gavaṛēśvaradēva of the agrahāra of Savasi (also referred to as Tapasi-grāma) by the Four-Hundred Mahājanas who are praised in the beginning. It also records a gift of income from certain taxes by the Five-Hundred Svāmis of Ayyāvoḷe and the One Thousand Tambuligas to the same deity, made over to Īśānaśakti-paṇḍita, an ācārya of the Kāḷāmukha sect. The record which contains an eulogy of these svāmis seems to register another gift on the second date. But the details are all lost.

cells.dynasty: Bijjala · Bijjala
cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: This record is dated the cyclic year Pārthiva, Kārtika, śu. Monday, Saṃkramaṇa Neither the Śaka nor the regnal year of the king is given. The tithi also is omitted. The cyclic year Pārthiva which occurred during the reign of Bijjala coincided with A. D. 1165 and the Śukla-paksha of Kārtika fell in October. In that paksha occurred two Mondays, one on the 11th and the other on the 18th of October. There was no Saṃkramaṇa on either of the days. In the absence of the tithi it is not possible to determine as to which of the two Mondays was intended. The inscription records a grant of land made by Kēśava-daṇḍanāyaka, the officer in charge of taxes (suṅkādhikāri) for the benefit of the temple of God Brahmēśvaradēva, attached to that of the God Chikēśvaradēva of Baḷḷarabiḍu. The grant was made in the presence of the karaṇas, headed by Siddhughidaṇḍanāyaka, Hariharagāvuṇḍa, heggaḍe Biraṇa and others and was entrusted to Vimalaśaktidēva, the āchārya of the temple. The conquests of Bijjala are enumerated and the genealogy of Kēśava-daṇḍanāyaka is given.

cells.remarks: This record is dated in the cyclic year Vikṛita, Jyēṣṭha, Amāvāsyā, Monday. The king's regnal year is not given but the cyclic year Vikṛita which fell in the reign of Sōvidēva, coincided with A. D. 1170. In this year, the details of the date correspond regularly to Monday, June 15, f.d.t. ·10. The inscription records a gift of land to Dugga-jīya made by Daṇḍanāyaka Basavarasa, an officer of Mailaya-nāyaka, his brother Kopparasa, Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Vārarasa, the prabhu and gāvuṇḍas of Khēḍa, etc., out of the gift of 325 mattars of land which had been (formerly) made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kailāsarasa, a subordinate of Subhatuṅgadēva to the temple of Kailāsadēva at Khēḍa, the rājadhāni of the Thirtysix-village (division) included in Tarddavāḍi-nāḍu. It also registers the gift of an oil-mill to the same temple, by Daṇḍanāyaka Basavarasa and refers to a previous gift, apparently to the same temple, made by Babbagāvuṇḍa and Lakshmādēvi on the occasion of a solar eclipse.

The king is stated to have been ruling from Seleyahaḷḷi. 46 [ನೆಂ] ದಣ್ಣನಾಯಕಂ ಕುಮಾರ ಬಮ್ಮಿ ದೇವರೆಸರ್ ಕಂದು ಹ್ರಷ್ಟ ಪುಷ್ಟರಾಗಿ ಈ ಸ್ಥಳದೋರೇನಂ ಮಾಡಿದೋದಮ– 47 ಕ್ಷಯಫಲವೆಂಬುದಂ ಧರ್ಮಶಾಸ್ತ್ರಂಗಳಂ ತಿಳಿದು ಈ ದೇವರ್ನಿನಿಯೋಗಕ್ಕೆ ತಮ್ಮ ಹೆಸರ ಧಮ್ಮF ವಾಗಿ ನ– 48 ದೇವನ್ನಾಗಿ ಭೂಮಿಯಂ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪಿಸಿ ಕುಡಪೇಳ್ದೆಂದು ವೀರವೆನೆ ಹಿಡಿದ ಧಮ್ಮFಮನೆ ಬಿಡುವಂ ತ್ಯಾಗಕ್ಕೆ ಕಲ್ಪ– 49 ವೃಕ್ಷವೆನಿಸಿದ * ಶ್ರೀಮನ್ಹಾ ಮಂಡಳೇಶ್ವರಂ ಎಳಮೇಲ ಸಿಂಗಿದೇವರೆಸನುಂ ತಾನುಂ ಏಕಭಾವದಿಂ ಸುಮನಸ್ಸರಾ– 50 ಗಿ ಶಕನೃಪಾಬ್ದಂ ೧೧೯ಳನೆಯ ನಂದನಸಂವತ್ಸರದ ಪುಷ್ಯ ಸುದ್ಧ ಲ ಸೋಮವಾರ ಉತ್ತರಾಯಣ ಸಂಕ್ರಾಂತಿ ವ್ಯತೀಪಾ– 51 ತಂ ಕೂಡಿದಲ್ಲ ಕಡಲೆವಾಡದ ಶ್ರೀ ಸ್ವಯಂಭುಸೋಮನಾಥದೇವಗೆ೯ ಮುನ್ನ ಕನಪಯ್ಯನಾಯ ಕನುಂ 52 ಸಿಂಗಿದೇವರೆಸಂಗೆ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಭೂಮಿಯೊಳಗಾಗಿ ಮೂಡರಾ ದೇವವಳ್ಳ ಸೆಂದೇವಾಡದ ಪಡುಣಾ ನೀಮೆ ಮೂಡ– 53 ಲಾಗಿ ತೆಂಕಲು ಕುಮಸೆಯ ಪ್ರಭುಮಾನ್ಯಂ ಮೇರೆ ಪಡುವಲು ದೇವಣಗಾವೆಯ ನೀಮೆ ಬಡಗಲಾ ನೀಮೆಯ 54 ಹಿಟ್ಟನೆತ್ತು ಗುಟ್ಟ ಕಡಲೆವಾಡದ ಪೂರ್ವ್ವಾದ ಚತುಃಸೀಮಾಪಾಟದೊಳಗೆ ನಿಧಿನಿಧಾನನಿಕ್ಷೇಪತರು ಪಥ– 55 ಮಾಲಾಏಕ್ಷಜಲಪಾಷಾಣಸಹಿತ ತ್ರಿಭೋಗಾಧ್ಯನ್ರವಾದಿಯಾಗಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಸ್ಥಳವಿತ್ತಿಯುಕ್ತ– 56 ತ್ರಿಯಂ ದೇವರ್ನಿನಿಯೋಗವೆನ್ನೆಂದಡೆ ತ್ರಿಕಾರಾಚ್ಯFನಾರಂಕಾರ ಮಹಾನ್ವೇದ್ಯಕ್ಮಂ ಕಪ್ಪರ್ನರ 57 ತಾಂಬೂಳಕುಂಕುಮಚಂದನಾನುಲೇಪನಕ್ಮಂ ಗೀತವಾದ್ಯನೃತ್ಯಕ್ಮಂ ಚೈತ್ರಪವಿತ್ರಾರೋಪಣಕ್ಮಂ ಬಂದ– 58 ತ್ಸುಚತಜೇಣ್ಣ Fದಾರ್ನರ ಸೋತೆಸುಣು ಮಾಟಕೂಟಕ್ಮಂ ತಪೋದನರತನತಾ (ಜ್ಞಾ) ದನಕೃವಾ ಚಂದ್ರಾಕ್ಕFಸ್ಥಾಯಿ– 59 ಯಾಗಿ ಯಮ ನಿಯಮಾಸನಪ್ರಾಣಾಯಾಮಪ್ರತ್ಯಾಹಾರಧ್ಯಾನಧಾರಣಮೋನಾನುಷ್ಠಾ[ನ] ಜಪನಮಾಧಿಶೀಲಗುಣಸಂಪನ್ರರುಂ ವಿಬುಧಜನಮೋತ್ಸಿತ್ಥಫಲಸಮುತ್ಪನ್ನರುಂ ದೀನಾನಾಥಜತರ ರದಾ– 61 ವಫಾವಕನಿವಾರಣರುಂ ದುರಿತಮಡಗನಿವಾರಣರುಂ ನಿಜಸಮಯತರಣಯ್ತು ರಕ್ಷದಕ್ಷರುಂ ಅನ್ನ[ನ]– 62 ವರತಸುಭಿಕ್ಷರುಂ ಪಣ್ಣಿ ತಚೂಡಾಮಣಿಯುಂ ನಿಷ್ಪ ಜನಚಿನ್ಮಾಮಣಿಯುಂ ಇತ್ಯಾದಿ ನಾಮಾವಳೀ ವಿರಾಜಿತ– 63 ರುಮಪ್ಪ ಶ್ರೀಮದಲ್ಲಾಚಾರ್ಯ್ಕರು ಸೋವರಾಸಿಪಣ್ಣ ತದೇವಗೆ೯ ದಾರಾಪೂರ್ವಕಂ ಮಾಡಿ ಕೊಟ್ಟರು (0) 64 ಗೋಚಮ್ಮFಮಾತ್ರಭೂಮಿಯ ಧೂಚಕ್ರದೊಳತ್ತ ವಗ್ಗೆ ಸ್ವಗ್ಗ Fಫಲಂ ತಾನಾ ಚಮ್ಮF ಮಾರಿದಂ– 65 ದಂದಿನಾ ಚಮ್ಮFನ್ಸರದ ನಸಿಯ ಬೇಗ್ಗ ಳ ಪವನ || ವರೆವಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮ ಕಡಿತಂ ಧ[ರ್ರೆ] ಬಳಪಂ ಹಿಮಗಿರೆಂದ್ರವಾದೊಡ– 66 ವೇನುಂ ನಿರುತಂ ಲೆಕ್ಕನೆಣ이ುಮ ಪರಮದ ಮುಂದೊಮ್ಮೆ ಮಾಲ್ವ ಭೋಗದ ಫಲಮಂ || ಇದ ರಕ್ಷಿಪಂಗೆ ಸಾಶ್ವತ ಪದವಿಗ– 67 ಲದಿಗೋಳು ವಿದುಟೊಳನೆಯಂ ಮಾಡುವಂಗೊದವಿ ದಾರವನರದ ಪುಳ್ಳ ಕೊಳದ್ದಿ ಕ್ಯು ಕ ಲ್ಪಕೋಟಿ ಸ– 68 ಹಸ್ರಂ || © ಶ್ರೀಮದಲ್ಲಾಚಾರ್ಯ್ಕರು ಸೋವರಾಸಿಪಣ್ಣ ತದೇವರು ತಮ್ಮ ಪುತ್ರ ಶ್ರೀ ಸೋಮ ನಾಥದೇವ– 69 ಪಾದಾರಾಧಕಂ ಸರಸ್ವತೀದೇವೀಲಬ್ಧಪ್ರಸಾದಂ ಪ್ರಾsನಾದಮಾಟಕೂಟಪ್ರವೀಣನಪ್ಪ 70 ಸೂತ್ರಧಾರಿ ಸಂಗೋಜಂಗೆಯಲ್ಲದು ದನದವಂ ಕೆಯ್ಯನಿಪ್ಪು ತು ಕಯ್ಯು ನಿವೇಷನವಿಷ್ಮ[ತು]

cells.remarks: This record is dated Śaka 1097, Manmatha, Pushya, ba. Amāvāsyā, Tuesday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṁkrānti, corresponding to A. D. 1176, January 13, Tuesday. The saṁkrānti did not, however, occur on that day. The inscription states that Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Siṁgidēvarasa of Eḷamēlu, belonging to the Silāhāra family, Kasapayya-nāyaka, Mahāpradhāna, Daṇḍanāyaka Kumāra Bammidēvarasa, śrīkaraṇa Chākaṇayya-nāyaka, the mahāprabhu of Kummasi, Guṇḍarasa and his brother Mahādēvarasa made a gift of land and certain taxes for the worship and offerings to the temple of Svayambhū Sōmanātha. The gift was entrusted to āchārya Sōvarāsidēva. The king is stated to have been ruling from Maṅgaḷivēḍa.

cells.location: HIRĒ BĒVINŪR, INDI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT — Karnataka

cells.dynasty: Bhillama · Bhillama
cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: This record is dated Śaka 1112 (nara-nētra-Śaśi-Sōma-Indu), Sādhāraṇa, Śrāvaṇa, Pūrṇimā, Thursday, corresponding to A. D. 1190, July 18. The week-day was Wednesday, when the tithi ended at 72. The inscription states that at the request of Siridēvi, the wife of Boppaṇa-nāyaka, to observe kshitiruha-nōṁpi, Daṇḍanāyaka Māyidēva, the minister of the king, planted a number of trees and established a charity fair (dharma-santhe) in Bēvinūr situated in Tardavāḍi 1000, in the presence of Mummuridaṇḍas and others of the Thirty-six-villages division. Boppaṇa-nāyaka was governing the division of Thirty-six-villages as a subordinate of Māyidēva. It also records a gift of land and house for the maintenance of the above charities made to Bandarasa, the manneya of Tarddavāḍi-1000 and to Boppaṇanāyaka by Māyidēva. Further gifts of trees to the temples of Taleyakāvadēva, Rēvaṇēśvara and Bhōgēśvara and also to Sōmanātha-paṇḍita, the composer of the record, are registered.

cells.remarks: This record is dated Śaka 1115, Paridhāvi, Bhādrapada, ba. Madhyāṣṭaki, Monday, Kanyā-saṁkramaṇa. The Śaka year given was current. The details correspond to A. cells.dynasty: Singhaṇa · Siṅghaṇa
cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: This record is dated in the king's regnal year 32, Śarvari, Chaitra, ba. 11, Wednesday, corresponding to A.D. 1240, March 20, which was a Tuesday and not Wednesday. The tithi ended on that day at .92. The inscription is in two parts. The first part, in Sanskrit language, records the gift of six nivartanas of land for the benefit of the temple of Durgā at Kundamguḷa by Mallasarma, son of Basavaṇa and grandson of Mādhavārya, with the consent of the king's minister Vāsudēva. The record was composed by Vaijanātha. The latter part of the inscription, written in Kannada language, apparently refers to the same gift mentioned above. The donor is called here Taliyara Mallayya. It also records a gift of oil made by the Fifty-Families (Aivattokkalu) of Kuindungola, for burning a perpetual lamp in the same temple. The Thousand Mahājanas of Kuindungula were to protect the gifts.

cells.remarks: This damaged record is dated in the year Śarvari, Jyeṣṭha śu. Monday, Solar eclipse. The Śaka year is lost except the last digit which is 2. Śarvari corresponds with Śaka 1162 but the existing details are irregular. The paksha given, viz., Śuddha is apparently wrong because of the mention of the solar eclipse. Again, in the month of Jyeṣṭha of the given year there was no eclipse at all. In the previous month however, i. e. Nija-Vais'ākha, both the lunar and solar eclipses occurred on Monday, the 7th and Wednesday, the 23rd respectively in May, A.D. 1240. The intended date seems to be A. D. 1240, May 23. The inscription mentions Mahāpradhāna, Sēnādhipati Bommeyanāyaka.

cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: This record is dated Śaka 1167, Krōdhi, Bhādrapada, śu. 14, Sunday. The date is irregular. Taking the Śaka year to be current (Krōdhi), the tithi corresponds to 1244 A. D., August 18. The week day was Thursday and not Sunday as stated in the record. This long inscription gives the genealogy of Singhaṇa and records gifts of lands and house-site by pradhāni Malla, Bichaṇa and his son Pāyiseṭṭi, for the benefit of the temple of Ananta-Tirthakara at Kalukere in Hagariṭage-nāḍu constructed by Pāyiseṭṭi, at the instance of his guru Kamalaśēna-bhaṭṭāraka. Pāyiseṭṭi, who is stated to be the son of Nākiseṭṭi, was given in adoption to Bichaṇa. Hagariṭage-nāḍu, Kalukere, Bichaṇa and his exploits, Pāyiseṭṭi and his brothers are all described at length.

cells.remarks: This record is dated in the king's regnal year 17, Prabhava, Mārgaśira, śu. 11 Monday. The details of the date are irregular. The year Prabhava coincides with A.D. 1207, but the details do not agree with that year. But in the previous year, i.e. Kshaya, the details regularly correspond to A.D. 1206, November 13, Monday, .06, which seems to be the intended date. According to this reckoning, the commencement of his reign would be A.D. 1190-91, one year earlier than the date suggested by Fleet (Bom. Gaz., Vol. I, Pt. II, p. 503). The inscription records a gift of land for the offerings to god Svayambhū Sōmanāthadēva and for the feeding of ascetics, by Hariyama-seṭṭi, the nāḷprabhu of Kalukere, in the presence of the Mummuridaṇḍas, Kācheya-sāhaṇi and Amiteyasāhaṇi. The gift was entrusted to Mūrujāvidēva. Supplementary gifts for the benefit of the same temple on Śivarātri and other occasions, are also recorded.

cells.location: BANAVĀSI, SIRSI TALUK, NORTH KANARA DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Slab set up to the left of Virabhadra shrine in the compound of the Madhukēśvara temple

cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: This record is dated Śaka 1290, Kīlaka, Vaiśākha, ba. 30, Monday, Solar eclipse. The date is irregular. In the given year the tithi corresponded to A.D. 1368, May 17, Wednesday (not Monday) and there was no eclipse on that day. It may be noted, however, that on Jyeshṭha ba. 30 of the following year i.e., Saumya, there occurred a solar eclipse when the tithi commenced on Monday at, .14 and lasted till .11 of Tuesday, the 5th June, A.D. 1369, when the solar eclipse occurred. The inscription states that when Mahāpradhāna Mādhavāṅka was governing Banavāsi 12000 province, Nāgappa, the son of Prabhu Śivadēva of Raṭṭakallu installed an image of god Virēśvara in the vicinity of Madhukanātha at Banavāsi, and made a grant of a village and money to the god. The grant was entrusted to Bikkidēva-oḍeya, the son of Lākuḷēśvaradēva-oḍeya. The latter is described as Kadambarāya-kul-āchārya. The king is stated to be ruling from Hastināvatipura.

The king is stated to be ruling from Hastināvati.

cells.remarks: There are two dates in this record. The first is dated Śaka 970, Sarvadhāri, Puṣya, ba. 7, Sunday, Uttarāyaṇa-saṃkrānti. The details given are irregular. The said tithi occurred on A.D. 1048, December 30, Friday when there was no saṃkrānti. In the previous year Sarvajit, the tithi corresponded to A.D. 1048, January 10. But there was no saṃkrānti on that day. The second date is Śaka 1009, Prabhava, Śrāvaṇa, Amāvāsyā, Sunday, solar eclipse, regularly corresponding to 1087 A.D., August 1. The inscription records the renewal of a former gift of land, which had lapsed, by the Raṭṭa Chief Kārtavīrya in conjunction with his wife Bhāgaladēvi to Jñānaśakti-vratīndra, disciple of Sōmēśvara-paṇḍitadēva of Puliyarasara-maṭha. It is also stated that Aṅkarasa was a feudatory of Trailōkyamalla (Sōmēśvara I). The record is damaged and worn out.

cells.remarks: This record is dated Chālukya-Vikrama year 54, Saumya, Chaitra śu. 2, Monday, Saṁkrānti. The tithi corresponds to A. D. 1129, March 23 which was Saturday. The Mēsha-saṁkrānti occurred on the next day. The inscription records a gift of land and money to god Kalidēvasvāmi of Sāsalu by Malliseṭṭi of Hulivara when Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Jayakēsidēva of the Kadamba family was governing Koṁkaṇa-900 and Palasige-12000 divisions. The gift land which was purchased by the donor from Sōmēśvara-bhaṭṭa, the son of Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa, the ūroḍeya of Sāsalu, and two others, was entrusted into the hands of Tējōrāśi-paṇḍita, the disciple of Dēvarāśi-paṇḍita, the āchārya of the temple. The record gives a genealogical account of the donor.

text.remarks: This record, in characters of about the 12th-13th Century A.D., registers the gift of oil from all the oil-mills of the village by Kētaiyya, son of Javaniseṭṭi, to Mu[re]ya-basadi of Gudigēre.

cells.location: KŌRVĀR, SINDGI TALUK, BIJAPUR DISTRICT — Karnataka
cells.place: Pillar built into the stone katte (raised platform) in front of Daṇḍappa Gauḍa's house
cells.dynasty: Siṅghaṇa · Siṅghaṇa
cells.language: Kannada
cells.remarks: This badly damaged and effaced record is dated in Śaka 1133, Prajāpati, Kārtika, Amāvāsya, Sunday, Saṁkramaṇa, corresponding to A. D. 1211, November 6 Sunday, f.d.t.·27. This inscription seems to record a gift (of land) made to the learned mahājanas of Sāntheya Kō[rā]vūr, for the merit of a certain Bommarasa.
